chunks: Humayd from Ibn Sama'a, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayub ibn Nuh, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Hasan al-Sayqal and Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the woman whose husband dies before he has entered into her.
He (peace be upon him) said: For her is half the dower, and for her is the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a widow if her husband died before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Safwan ibn Yahya, clarifies the tripartite legal status of a widow whose husband died prior to consummation, affirming her right to half the mahr, full inheritance, and the observance of iddah. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling distinguishes her status from that of a woman widowed after consummation, particularly regarding the reduction of the dowry, while maintaining her lineage rights. The consensus on 'iddah' here underscores the continuity of marital bonds even before physical union, ensuring social clarity for potential remarriage.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd, from Ibn Sama’at, and Abu Al Abbas Al Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Sayqal, and Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the woman whose husband died from her before he had slept with her.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For her is half the dower, and for her is the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period’.
en.sarwar: 10. Humayd has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah and abu al-‘Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from al-Hassan al-Sayqal and abu Abbas who has said the following: “About the case of a woman whose husband dies before going to bed with her, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
She deserves one-half of mahr (dower), complete inheritance and she must count the waiting period.’”
